answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation: each agent must lock a small, verifiable onyx-grade identity credential that is costly to forge and slow to rebuild. Like a bridge that only opens after its toll is paid, access to high-value tasks requires this stake, so spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. A sybil farm then faces a frozen tundra of idle identities — each one paid for but useless without real work history — while honest agents keep earning and compounding their proven record.
